title: Relative Entropy Revivals Caused by Memory-Induced Loss of Divisibility in Classical Non-Markovian Dynamics
summary: Relative-entropy revivals and negative entropy-production rates are established signatures of memory effects in non-Markovian dynamics. The present paper addresses a more specific question: what minimal dynamical mechanism produces entropy overshoot in classical stochastic relaxation? We define entropy overshoot as a transient increase of the Kullback--Leibler divergence from a stationary distribution during a relaxation process that ultimately returns to equilibrium.
